CHIEF COMPLAINT
Exercise-induced asthma and mood concerns

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a school-aged student with asthma who recently attempted to join water polo. Reports difficulty breathing during physical activity that limits participation. Describes asthma symptoms including phlegm buildup in throat, coughing, chest tightness, and wheezing that occur with aerobic exercise such as running or water polo. Also experiences lightheadedness with exertion. Symptoms are triggered by every aerobic workout and are worsened by smoke exposure. Denies nighttime awakenings from asthma. Currently uses albuterol inhaler (2 puffs) as rescue medication, which alleviates symptoms within 15 minutes but requires sitting down to recover. Reports expected side effect of shakiness with inhaler use. Does not use any daily maintenance asthma medication. No other respiratory symptoms outside of activity or smoke exposure.

Additionally reports new-onset mood concerns beginning this school year. Describes stress related to SAT preparation and multiple AP classes. Reports significant sadness, lack of motivation, and fatigue. States he prefers to stay home rather than spend time with friends. Initially tried to join sports to feel more energized and happier. Denies specific difficulty with focus or information retention.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for seasonal allergies and fatigue. Negative for nighttime asthma awakenings, sleep disturbance, or other respiratory symptoms outside of exertion.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs as needed

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies noted

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
High school student with AP classes. Studying for SATs. Interested in water polo and sports. Active peer relationships.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert, no acute distress
Eyes: Normal
Ears: Minimal serous fluid noted bilaterally; otherwise normal
Throat: Normal, no tonsillar enlargement
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm
Abdomen: Normal bowel sounds, soft, nontender, no masses
Neurologic: Reflexes normal and symmetric

RESULTS
Minimal serous fluid in ears. Otherwise unremarkable physical examination.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Asthma, exercise-induced with possible allergic component: Start Singulair (montelukast) once daily as maintenance therapy. Expected improvement within approximately one month. Continue albuterol inhaler as rescue medication. Counseled that tremor is an expected side effect; recommend sitting down after use. Follow-up in 6 weeks to assess response to maintenance therapy.

Mood concerns, likely adjustment disorder related to academic stress: Referred to therapist for counseling. Will complete mood screening questionnaires. Follow-up in 2 weeks to discuss screening results and therapy progress.
